Bring Your A-Game — AI Agent Idea

DBLens

From database signals to answers — before they become incidents.

1What would you like to call your AI agent?

DBLens

2The problem

Database problems are a shared operational challenge across multiple application teams. When an application becomes slow, times out or database utilisation changes unexpectedly, engineers and DBAs must manually connect evidence across database metrics, Query Store, waits, blocking, execution plans, deployments, maintenance and pipeline activity. This increases time-to-diagnose, creates repeated investigation effort and consumes scarce DBA capacity. When a database change or specialist decision is then required, teams may also need Database CoE guidance or approval, adding further hand-offs and evidence preparation.

Opportunity: Move from “something is slow — start investigating and ask the DBA” to “DBLens has already correlated the signals, identified likely contributing factors, prepared the evidence and knows when specialist DBA or CoE involvement is required.”

3The solution

DBLens is an AI Database Reliability Agent that turns fragmented database telemetry, operational history and approved CoE knowledge into actionable intelligence. A colleague can ask, “Why has Staging been slow today?” DBLens gathers real telemetry, compares it with normal behaviour, analyses query regressions, waits, blocking and workload changes, and correlates them with deployments, maintenance or pipeline activity. It can also proactively surface emerging risks, compare symptoms with previous incidents and, where a recommended database change needs specialist governance, identify the relevant CoE guidance and prepare the evidence for review. AI handles investigation and preparation; DBAs and the Database CoE retain control of specialist decisions and approvals.

8What type of value will this AI agent create?

✓ Knowledge access✓ Automation✓ Decision support✓ Insights and analysis✓ Innovation✓ Capability building✓ Experience enhancement✓ Risk and governance
Business value: The primary value is improved database reliability: ↓ Mean Time to Diagnose · ↓ Mean Time to Resolve · ↓ repeated DBA/CoE effort · ↑ proactive risk visibility.

Illustratively, if 20 teams each have two database investigations per month, that is 480 investigations/year. Saving only 45 minutes of specialist investigation effort per case releases 360 hours — approximately 48 working days/year. At an illustrative £60/hour loaded cost, that is ~£21,600 annual capacity. Additional value can come from earlier detection, shorter incidents, fewer repeat issues, reduced application-team waiting time and better-prepared CoE engagements.

How we prove it: Baseline and measure Mean Time to Diagnose, Mean Time to Resolve, DBA escalations, investigation effort, repeat incidents, proactive issues identified, time spent collecting evidence, and CoE requests that arrive complete first time. These figures are scenario assumptions for pilot validation, not claimed savings.

9How many people will benefit from the outcomes created by this agent?

More than 50 colleagues — DBAs, Database CoE, application teams, support, testers and release teams benefit directly, with customers ultimately benefiting from faster diagnosis and more reliable services.
